content.text:
In the installed `agents` package, `MCPClientManager` doesn't take storage as a constructor argument. Its options are only `env` and `createAuthProvider`. It extends `LifecycleCapability` and gets storage through `this.lifecycle.storage`. When the host Lifecycle (an Agent or Durable Object) installs the capability, it supplies a `LifecycleServices` object whose `storage` field is the host Durable Object's `DurableObjectStorage`, i.e. its `ctx.storage`.

`onStart()` uses that storage to check the MCP schema version and create the MCP server table if needed (`node_modules/agents/dist/client-1tEQ1Oqz.js:1304-1306`). It then restores the persisted HTTP and RPC connections from the same storage. If the manager isn't installed on a Lifecycle, as in isolated unit tests, `lifecycleServices` is undefined, so there's no storage to use.

In the installed `agents` package, `MCPClientManager` doesn't take storage as a constructor argument. Its options are only `env` and `createAuthProvider`. It extends `LifecycleCapability` and gets storage through `this.lifecycle.storage`. When the host Lifecycle (an Agent or Durable Object) installs the capability, it supplies a `LifecycleServices` object whose `storage` field is the host Durable Object's `DurableObjectStorage`, i.e. its `ctx.storage`.

`onStart()` uses that storage to check the MCP schema version and create the MCP server table if needed (`node_modules/agents/dist/client-1tEQ1Oqz.js:1304-1306`). It then restores the persisted HTTP and RPC connections from the same storage. If the manager isn't installed on a Lifecycle, as in isolated unit tests, `lifecycleServices` is undefined, so there's no storage to use.
